raw_response:
I've been farming these 6 mu for 30 years now. Me and my wife, we're both around 50. Our son works in a factory in town, so it's mostly us two on the farm. He comes back to help at harvest time, but for daily work it's us.

This year I'll plant wheat on all 6 mu, same as always. I'll start planting around October 10th, right after the maize comes off. I buy the improved wheat seed from the agricultural shop in town — about 5 kg per mu. I used to save my own seed but the yield dropped after a few years, so now I buy new seed every two or three years. Costs me about 20 yuan per mu for the seed.

For fertilizer, I put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant the wheat. That's my base. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I spread another 45 jin of urea per mu. That's what I've always done. Last year I tried a bit less urea on one plot and the wheat looked yellow and the yield dropped, so I went back to my usual amount. I can't afford to use as much as Lao Wang down the road — he has 20 mu and more money — but I make sure I don't starve the crop. The compound gives some phosphorus and potassium too.

Irrigation... I have a well, but pumping costs money and electricity isn't cheap. For wheat I irrigate three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once in spring when it turns green, and once at jointing. If it's a really dry year maybe four times, but usually three is enough. I flood irrigate, same as everyone.

For maize, the summer crop, I plant it right after wheat harvest in early June. The window is tight — sometimes only 5 or 6 days between cutting wheat and planting maize. I always hire Old Zhang's tractor to plow quick, then we plant by hand with the small seeder. Maize gets compound fertilizer at planting and urea when the leaves are big. I irrigate maybe twice for maize, depending on the rain. If it's a wet summer like last year, maybe only once. Maize usually needs herbicide and sometimes insecticide if the corn borer comes.

Money is always tight with just 6 mu. I need to keep some cash for medicine, for daily expenses, for when things break. So I watch every yuan. But I also know from experience that if I don't put in enough fertilizer, I lose more money than I save. It's a balance. I aim for about 380 kg per mu of wheat and 420 kg per mu of maize. Not the highest in the village, but steady.
